decision: Take separate corporate existence out of the United Aircraft and Transport dissolution, issuing 521,883 shares to that company's holders
state_before: A stockholder group of a dissolving Delaware holding company; three plants in two countries
information_available: The approved Plan of Reorganization dated 1934-06-20; the joint-and-several guaranty; the 28,946 1/2-share warrant tail
unknowns: Whether the 1916 corporation was continued, renamed or bought; who negotiated
alternatives: Remain unincorporated; buy stock rather than assets
constraints: A guaranty shared by net worth 14.1155 / 55.0728 / 30.8117 percent; dissolution of the parent group
rationale: NOT STATED for this act - the stated rationales attach to the later collapses
expected_result: A going concern with an operating subsidiary and a public share register
actual_result: A company whose first four-month period lost 225,977.15 and whose own account began 1934-09-01

decision: Defer, rather than execute, the collapse of the Boeing Aircraft Company layer
state_before: Parent plus two direct subsidiaries plus a Canadian third layer
information_available: Officers of the parent take no salary; the parent's only expenses are taxes, legal, audit, transfer agent, registrar and stock certificates
unknowns: Cost and timing; tax computation of an asset transfer
alternatives: Collapse at once; sell Stearman; merge into an airline
rationale: 'In order to simplify management and taxation problems' the board had under consideration acquiring the assets of Boeing Aircraft Company and possibly Stearman
actual_result: Stearman went first (1938); the aircraft-company step was forecast for 1936, again for 1938, and is NOT printed as completed inside the window

decision: Buy roughly 28 acres adjoining Boeing Field instead of acquiring an existing factory
state_before: Small-volume production with a multi-engine trend
information_available: The demonstrated efficiency of large multi-engined aircraft; the site has rail and waterway connections
alternatives: Build away from the airport; lease
constraints: 'These plans for improved facilities will not require additional capital'
rationale: Assemble large aircraft efficiently, adjacent to a public airport
actual_result: Plant No. 2 built 1936-37, then expanded by 667,000 and roughly 974,000 square feet in 1940 to a three-plant Seattle total near 2,344,500 square feet

decision: RENT university research capacity rather than build it: a part-time rental contract for the University of Washington high-speed wind tunnel
information_available: The tunnel is under construction in Seattle
alternatives: Build in-house; proceed without; use a government laboratory
constraints: A loss year with a capital-light expansion policy chosen the same month
rationale: 'an excellent laboratory for advanced aerodynamic research and testing'
actual_result: Hired capability became owned staff by FY1939: additions to technical, aerodynamic and flight research departments

decision: Fund through a RIGHTS ISSUE to existing holders rather than new outside equity
state_before: Deficit years 1934-35; a four-engine programme about to be priced at a contract price
information_available: 173,424 shares placed: 163,847 on exercise of rights, 9,577 taken up by underwriters
unknowns: The rights price and subscription detail - the layer's tables are column-damaged
alternatives: Bank borrowing (used instead in 1938-39); a private placement; retrenchment
constraints: Loss years make new outside holders expensive to court; an unpaid officer class at the parent
rationale: Not stated in the legible columns
expected_result: Cash without a change of control
actual_result: 5.5 percent of the issue landed with underwriters; the same pattern in 1940 at 24.5 percent, on a much larger issue

decision: Convert The Stearman Aircraft Company into a DIVISION of the parent
state_before: Wichita operating profitably as a subsidiary corporation
information_available: The 1934-35 intention on the record; Stearman's own results
unknowns: Stearman holders' acceptance; the tax computation
constraints: as proposed in last year's annual report
expected_result: A division of the parent with the same order book
actual_result: A division at the boundary; its Wichita output doubled under federal contract, and Flying Fortress parts transferred there from Seattle in 1940

decision: KEEP Boeing Aircraft of Canada in operation instead of liquidating, and simultaneously begin disposal for nationality reasons
state_before: Dormant, boat repair, minority capital wiped, estimated liquidation loss not in excess of 200,000
information_available: Reorganisation of management and reduced overhead; unfilled orders at a multi-year high
alternatives: Liquidate; sell to Canadian interests; leave dormant
constraints: A British and Canadian rule placing rearmament contracts only with nationally controlled companies; 6 percent preferred dividends in arrears since December 1, 1930
rationale: Two contradictory stated aims in one report: continue 'for the time being' (1935) and dispose because it 'appears desirable' (1938)
expected_result: A profitable Canadian operation, or a clean exit
actual_result: Neither: still wholly owned at FY1940 with a Government-built leased plant, a small Canadian profit and 231,730 Canadian dollars of preferred arrears

state_before: Nine-month loss of 2,606,106; delivery schedules out of line with contractual obligations; a stockholder letter on the condition of the companies dated 1939-11-24
information_available: The backlog series, the Clipper and Stratoliner cost position, the authority for a 5,500,000 facility
unknowns: Who was replaced and on what terms; whether Egtvedt's chairmanship is the same act; no board minute is held
alternatives: Retrench; sell; replace engineering rather than management
constraints: A deficit about to be written off against paid-in surplus; two live bombardment contracts
rationale: 'to bring delivery schedules into line with contractual obligations'
actual_result: FY1940 reports the objectives met, production substantially increased, and the first profit - though the same report discloses that 163,000 of pre-tax income came from a policy change

decision: Increase authorised capital from 800,000 to 1,250,000 shares and hold a rights offer in reserve
state_before: A deficit of 3,471,686.29 about to be eliminated against paid-in surplus
information_available: A bank facility then being arranged
unknowns: 'No definite program has been adopted by the Directors'
alternatives: Borrow against the plants; sell the Canadian subsidiary
constraints: Mortgages and assigned contract proceeds already bank terms
rationale: To be able to act 'as soon as conditions make such an offering advisable'
actual_result: Used within five months: 360,496 shares at $16.00, net 5,392,547.25, retiring the loan

decision: Take the Government's emergency plant money instead of funding expansion from the rights proceeds
state_before: Unencumbered plants only days after repaying the bank loan in full
information_available: Note 3's terms in full: 60-month reimbursement, ceilings of 7,625,000 and 3,625,000 with construction-period interest, termination options, bank recourse confined to Government payments, notes payable to July 1, 1946
unknowns: Whether other manufacturers were offered the same terms; the interest rate
alternatives: Self-fund from equity; refuse the programme
constraints: A National Defense programme with published allocation of work to this firm
rationale: 'In order to assist in expediting the National Defense program'
actual_result: 3,033,461.35 expended and 2,240,445.62 borrowed by December 31, 1940 - the encumbrance the company had just removed returns in a different form

decision: Change accounting policy so that allocated general, administrative and engineering research cost sits in work in process
state_before: In prior years such cost went directly to profit and loss - i.e. it landed in loss years
information_available: The inventory ceiling rule and the roughly 163,000 quantified both by management and by the auditors
unknowns: Whether the change was permitted, required or chosen
constraints: An inventory that may not exceed proportionate sales value
rationale: 'the desirable effect of having the Profit and Loss statement reflect the true cost of a project in the same period in which the income therefrom is taken up'
actual_result: First reported profit, with 28.9 percent of pre-tax income attributable to the change (DERIVED), disclosed by the auditors themselves
